takeaways: Cut to new visual on every 2‑second beat of the background track
Use a sliding “map‑wipe” transition that follows a line‑path over the still photo or clip
Overlay kinetic type that animates in‑sync with a metronome‑style click (letter‑by‑letter or word‑by‑word)
Apply a duotone or high‑contrast colour filter to all assets for instant visual cohesion
Introduce a thin, animated border or underline that tracks the cursor‑like path of the map line
Layer a semi‑transparent “stat‑card” that slides in from the side, stays 3‑seconds, then snaps out
Add a subtle pulse or scale‑pop to key words or icons at the moment of a narrative punchline
Keep the aspect ratio 9:16 and use full‑bleed stills; crop any extra space with a vignette to keep focus on the centre action
avoid: Over‑loading the screen with more than three type layers at once
Using stock music without a clear beat to sync cuts
Full‑screen static text without any motion or visual cue
styles_to_watch: Map‑Line Reveal – a thin animated line that draws routes or outlines while the camera pans across a static map
Beat‑Synced Kinetic Typography – type that jumps, rotates or scales exactly on each beat of a tight soundtrack
Duotone Split‑Screen – two contrasting colour tones split the screen, each side showing a related still or clip
Stat‑Card Pop‑In – a compact info card that slides in, pulses, then exits as the narration hits a key fact
